name: pd-customer-rif-notifications
what_it_holds: Python script that scrapes the layoffs.fyi Airtable backend directly and posts row information to a Slack channel — demonstrates a working, minimal API-based pull method for layoffs.fyi's underlying Airtable rather than screen-scraping the site.
why_useful: A lightweight, working recipe for pulling layoffs.fyi data programmatically (via its Airtable API) which could be re-run periodically to build our own point-in-time vintage register of headcount events, addressing the point-in-time problem noted for this whole data family.
themes: Airbnb corporate footprint signals: careers/Greenhouse job-posting scrapers, LinkedIn headcount trackers, layoffs.fyi data, Glassdoor/Indeed review datasets, GitHub org activity (GH Archive)
why_all: A lightweight, working recipe for pulling layoffs.fyi data programmatically (via its Airtable API) which could be re-run periodically to build our own point-in-time vintage register of headcount events, addressing the point-in-time problem noted for this whole data family.

name: linkedin-employee-count-scraper
what_it_holds: A scraper aimed at pulling LinkedIn company employee-count figures (headcount) — no committed dataset, 0 stars, unclear if still functional against LinkedIn's current anti-scraping measures.
why_useful: If it still works, LinkedIn's 'employees on LinkedIn' counter is a widely-used informal headcount proxy for public companies including Airbnb; but this repo shows no evidence of being maintained or of holding any data, and scraping LinkedIn directly would be a terms-of-service question requiring human sign-off per repo rules.

name: tenacious-conversion-engine
what_it_holds: A lead-generation system that ingests 'public signal data (Crunchbase, job posts, layoffs.fyi)' to score companies — built for a benchmark eval, not a data repository per se; no dataset files confirmed.
why_useful: Shows a pattern for combining job-posting counts + layoffs signal + Crunchbase into a single 'company health' score, which is conceptually close to what a headcount-momentum indicator for Airbnb would need, but this repo itself has no committed Airbnb-relevant data.
